Green Tamales

Served at: Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe

Serves 8Prep 45 minCook 1 hour 15 min

Green Tamales are a traditional Mexican dish often served during the Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe on December 12th. These tamales are filled with a flavorful green salsa made from tomatillos and green chilies, symbolizing renewal and hope during this important religious celebration.

Ingredients

  • 4 cups (500 g) masa harina
  • 2 cups (480 ml) chicken broth, warm
  • 1 cup (225 g) lard or vegetable shortening
  • 1 teaspoon baking powder
  • 1 teaspoon salt
  • 2 cups (300 g) cooked shredded chicken
  • 20 fresh tomatillos, husked and rinsed
  • 3-4 jalapeño peppers, stemmed and seeded
  • 1 medium white onion, quartered
  • 3 garlic cloves
  • 1 cup (30 g) fresh cilantro leaves
  • 1 teaspoon ground cumin
  • Salt to taste
  • 30-40 dried corn husks, soaked in warm water for 30 minutes

Method

  1. Soak the dried corn husks in warm water for at least 30 minutes to soften.
  2. In a blender, combine tomatillos, jalapeños, onion, garlic, cilantro, cumin, and salt; blend until smooth to make the green salsa.
  3. Pour the salsa into a saucepan and simmer over medium heat for 10-15 minutes to thicken slightly; set aside to cool.
  4. In a large bowl, beat the lard or shortening until fluffy.
  5. Add masa harina, baking powder, and salt to the lard and mix well.
  6. Gradually add warm chicken broth to the masa mixture, beating continuously until a soft dough forms; the dough should be light and spreadable.
  7. Mix about 1 cup of the green salsa into the masa dough to give it a green tint and flavor.
  8. Spread a thin layer of the green masa dough onto the smooth side of each soaked corn husk, about 2 tablespoons per husk.
  9. Place a spoonful of shredded chicken in the center of the masa on each husk.
  10. Top the chicken with a small spoonful of the remaining green salsa.
  11. Fold the sides of the husk in toward the center, then fold the bottom up to enclose the filling securely.
  12. Place the tamales upright in a steamer basket over boiling water.
  13. Cover with a damp cloth and steam for about 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes, or until the masa is firm and pulls away easily from the husks.
  14. Let tamales rest for 10 minutes before serving.

Tips

  • If you prefer a milder tamale, reduce the number of jalapeños or remove seeds completely.
  • Serve with extra green salsa or crema for added flavor.
  • For a vegetarian version, substitute the chicken with cooked mushrooms or roasted vegetables.
